title: Run a long worker's adapter off the Body's turn so one worker no longer freezes every other mission (S38-A)
problem: Directive 2026-10-28 section 38 (gap-map unit S38-A, 'Non-blocking worker dispatch: a long worker must not freeze every other mission'). On #196's head 3a2ba265 MissionEngine._pursue calls AuthorityOffice.act inline; for worker.commission the Gate calls the provider adapter and waits for it, inside Body.tick. While a worker runs (minutes for a frontier worker), every other mission, the inbox (only BODY_STOP is read) and the heartbeat stop. Reproduced by tests/unit/test_greg_background_dispatch.py::test_a_long_worker_does_not_freeze_the_other_missions on the base: the quick mission never closes while the worker holds (timed out after 30 s).
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (section 38; gap-map unit S38-A in acceptance/directive-sections.json)
Directive 2026-10-14 section 3A: 'long-running missions, asynchronous workers, temporary teams, unattended computation'; section 3C: 'Durable job management'
INTENT-20261014-ONE-MACHINE (one Body, one constitutional consequence path; no second execution authority)
baseline: 3a2ba265: the adapter runs inside the turn. Write-ahead intent (mission.dispatching) plus the Gate's claim already make a body killed inside office.act recoverable (MissionEngine._recover_dispatch).

alternatives.name: Proposed: only the adapter leaves the turn (greg/background.py)
alternatives.description: Body.tick holds a turn lock for the whole turn. For a capability in BACKGROUND_CAPABILITIES (worker.commission), _pursue runs the Gate's whole act on a thread that holds the same lock, except inside the adapter, which a wrapper runs unlocked. The turn waits until the adapter has started (or the act ended without it, which is then recorded exactly as inline), and goes on. A mission whose adapter still runs is not stepped (WORKING). The outcome is recorded by _record_outcome on the dispatch's thread under the lock, with the mission re-read from the ledger and the completion time. Enabled by Body.run only; tick() callers keep dispatching inline.
advantages: Gate, AuthorityOffice, MissionBook and journal stay single-threaded: only the adapter body runs beside a turn
Crash, STOP and reconciliation semantics are the existing ones (write-ahead intent, claim without receipt -> UNCERTAIN)
No ledger record type and no Gate change; 2 engine sites changed
Every turn-by-turn test keeps its exact inline behaviour
disadvantages: A turn lock is new shared state; a future code path that writes the ledger outside a turn without it would race
Background mode is exercised only by Body.run (process tests and the new thread test), not by the many tick()-driven tests
A signed BODY_STOP reaches a running worker only after a turn ingests it (the main loop wakes on a new inbox file)

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: shorter worker timeouts
alternatives.description: Bound every worker so a turn never waits long.
disadvantages: Caps what a worker can do; the body still freezes for the bound
alternatives.revival_evidence: If background dispatch shows a defect that cannot be bounded.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing design: a durable job model (start, poll, collect as separate receipted steps)
alternatives.description: worker.commission becomes start (receipted STARTED with a job id) and a later collect step; the Gate learns a two-phase act.
advantages: Survives a restart without reconciliation: a running job can be re-adopted
disadvantages: Changes the Gate's act contract, the canonical consequence path, and the receipt shape every reader binds to
A re-adopted job needs supervision outside the body process (PDEATHSIG no longer applies)
alternatives.revival_evidence: When workers must outlive a body restart (founder ruling) or run on another node (section 48 nodes).

alternatives.name: Run each mission's whole step on a thread
disadvantages: The engine, book and office are not thread-safe; races everywhere

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: One worker freezes the body for its duration; section 38 stays unmet.
disadvantages: Every mission, the inbox and the heartbeat stop while a worker runs
A long worker reads to Mission Control as a hung body

roles.position: Section 38 and the 2026-10-14 directive's asynchronous workers: the body keeps pursuing its other goals while one worker runs. No authority changes: the same Gate admits, claims and receipts the same act.
material_concerns: A pause no longer catches every dispatch mid-flight: a worker already running finishes (STOP still interrupts it). Recorded as a founder ruling.

roles.position: Smallest change that meets the effect: one module, two engine sites, the Body's turn. No second execution path: the background act is the same office.act call.
material_concerns: The turn lock must cover every ledger write outside the turn in Body.run (note_gap, telemetry, heartbeat, body.stopped): done

roles.position: Attacked: a stop predicate that writes the ledger off the turn (fixed: _stop_flag is lock-free), a busy mission mistaken for a killed dispatch (fixed: not stepped while busy), an error after hand-off swallowed (fixed: raised by the next turn), a body that records it stopped before its workers recorded (fixed: join first).
material_concerns: Integrator intake review: a mission whose own background outcome landed mid-turn was stepped from the copy sorted before that record (fixed: the turn rebuilds and re-reads after any off-turn record)

Integrator intake review: a body ending on an error neither joined nor stopped its running workers before closing the ledger (fixed: Body.close shuts down every dispatch, kills a non-polling worker's process group, then closes under the turn lock)

Integrator intake review: a cancel or detach ingested while a worker ran did not reach it (fixed: it interrupts the worker; a pause, DECISION or DEVICE_REVOKE does not change an act the Gate already admitted)

roles.position: The heartbeat names WORKING missions (also while paused); body.stopped names dispatches still unfinished after the join timeout.
material_concerns: Threads make failures harder to read; the dispatch thread is named after its mission and action

roles.position: Nothing is recorded for a dispatch that is still running; the outcome is recorded once, from the Gate's receipt, at its completion time.
material_concerns: Spend of the running worker is reserved only by the write-ahead and the Gate's claim, as inline

evidence.claim: The freeze reproduces on base and is gone on the branch
evidence.finding: Base (greg/body.py, greg/missions.py at 3a2ba265): failed, the quick mission never closed while the worker held (30 s). Branch: passed; the worker's outcome is recorded once, after it returned; the chain verifies.

evidence.claim: An error after the hand-off kills the next turn
evidence.finding: Raised by the next tick; the write-ahead intent stays for the restart

evidence.claim: Intake review items fixed, each with a test that fails on the pre-fix code
evidence.finding: On d04b2563's greg/: 6 of the new tests fail (stale step state 0.00 vs 0.01 booked; worker child alive after an error close; non-polling worker not killed; cancel, supersede and detach not interrupting). With the fixes: all 9 pass

counterevidence.claim: STOP and SIGKILL during a background worker are covered only by the existing process tests
counterevidence.finding: They drive Body.run, so they now run the background path; no new STOP test was written

pass_1.intended_outcome: While one worker runs, every other mission is stepped, the inbox is read and the heartbeat moves; the worker's act is admitted, receipted and reconciled exactly as before.

advantages.statement: Other missions progress during a worker
advantages.amplified_value: Persistent goal pursuit holds with paid workers in flight; reverses if a race corrupts the ledger, bounded by the turn lock

advantages.statement: Existing crash and reconciliation semantics reused
advantages.amplified_value: No new recovery path to prove; a killed body is settled by _recover_dispatch as before

disadvantages.statement: New shared state: the turn lock
disadvantages.redesigned_response: One plain Lock, held by Body.tick for a whole turn and by a background dispatch everywhere but inside its adapter; every other Body.run ledger write (note_gap, telemetry, heartbeat, body.stopped) takes it; documented in greg/background.py

disadvantages.statement: A pause no longer catches a dispatch mid-flight; a running worker finishes
disadvantages.redesigned_response: STOP still interrupts a running worker (lock-free _stop_flag); whether a pause should too is recorded as a founder ruling; the heartbeat names running work while paused

disadvantages.statement: Only Body.run exercises the background path
disadvantages.redesigned_response: A thread test drives Body.run with a real clock; the process tests that drive Body.run (one-machine, attacks, mid-flight kill) now run the background path

pass_2.attack_summary: Attacked the Pass-1 design for writes outside the lock, a stale mission state at record time, lost errors, ordering of the stop record and in-flight missions being re-dispatched or settled.

new_weaknesses.statement: Body._stop_now reads the inbox (writes the ledger) and was the adapter's stop check
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Background adapters get _stop_flag, which only reads flags and the stop file

new_weaknesses.statement: The outcome would be recorded against the mission state of the dispatching turn
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: finish() re-reads the mission from the ledger and uses the completion time when the adapter ran off the turn

new_weaknesses.statement: body.stopped could precede a running worker's outcome
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Body.run joins every dispatch first (60 s on STOP); unfinished ones are named on body.stopped

new_weaknesses.statement: Same-turn stale state: MissionEngine.tick sorted copies once; while it handed one worker off, another mission's background outcome could record (and rebuild the book), and that mission was then stepped from its pre-record copy (committed spend 0.00 against 0.01 booked)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Background.recorded counts off-turn records; tick rebuilds the book when it moved and steps each mission from book.missions; failing-first test tests/unit/test_greg_background_dispatch.py::test_a_mission_stepped_after_its_own_background_outcome_landed_mid_turn_reads_the_recorded_state

new_weaknesses.statement: Shutdown and error paths: Body.close ran without the turn lock and without a join, so a dispatch could append after body.stopped or race ledger.close, and a worker child could outlive the body
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Background.shutdown stops every adapter (closing flag in its stop predicate), joins, kills the process groups of live supervised children (greg.workers.kill_live_workers) when an adapter stopped polling, and joins again; Body.close calls it on every exit path, then closes the ledger under the turn lock; failing-first tests tests/unit/test_greg_background_dispatch.py::test_a_body_closing_on_an_error_stops_and_records_its_running_worker_before_the_ledger_closes and tests/unit/test_greg_background_dispatch.py::test_a_worker_that_ignores_its_stop_has_its_process_group_killed_when_the_body_closes

new_weaknesses.statement: Commands mid-run: turns keep ingesting commands while a worker runs, but a cancel of its mission or a detach of its capability did not reach it
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: MissionEngine.interrupt_withdrawn (every turn, paused too) interrupts the dispatch through Background.stop_for and records mission.dispatch_interrupted once; the worker stops and its outcome is UNCERTAIN, reconciled; pause, BODY_PAUSE, DECISION and DEVICE_REVOKE do not interrupt (documented, pinned by tests/unit/test_greg_background_dispatch.py::test_a_pause_while_the_worker_runs_does_not_interrupt_the_admitted_act); failing-first test tests/unit/test_greg_background_dispatch.py::test_a_founder_cancel_or_detach_while_the_worker_runs_interrupts_it

residual_risks.risk: A future ledger writer outside a turn and without the lock
residual_risks.mitigation: Documented in greg/background.py and greg/body.py; kill criterion on any broken chain
residual_risks.review_trigger: Any new thread or timer in greg/

residual_risks.risk: A dispatch still running after shutdown (its adapter neither polls nor runs a supervised child)
residual_risks.mitigation: Named on body.stopped (dispatches_unfinished); Body.close then closes the ledger under the turn lock, so its late record fails instead of interleaving; settled on restart by _recover_dispatch

residual_risks.risk: kill_live_workers kills every supervised child of the process, not only this body's
residual_risks.mitigation: Called only by a closing body after its join timeout; one body runs per process

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Bounded by one lock that covers every writer outside the adapter
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: A new ledger writer outside Body.tick

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Pause semantics during a running worker are the founder's
Inline remains the behaviour of turn-by-turn callers; the background path has thread and process tests
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: A defect found only on the background path

pass_2.final_design: Only the adapter of a BACKGROUND_CAPABILITIES dispatch (worker.commission) runs off the Body's turn, enabled by Body.run; the Gate's admission, claim, commit and receipt and the outcome record stay serialized under the turn lock; a busy mission is not stepped; errors after hand-off are raised by the next turn; STOP reaches the adapter lock-free and the Body joins before recording it stopped. After intake review: each mission is stepped from the book as it is after any off-turn record; every exit path stops and joins running dispatches (process groups killed if an adapter stops polling) before the ledger closes under the turn lock; a founder cancel or a capability leaving ATTACHED interrupts the running worker.

dissent.handling: Recorded; does not block the draft.

entries.position: Should a signed BODY_PAUSE also interrupt a running worker (as STOP does), turning it into a reconciliation?
entries.rationale: A pause is 'suspend'; a paid worker continuing to spend while paused may surprise the founder

authority_impact.approver: None for this draft experiment; adoption into #196 by its integrator, and any merge, remain Alfonso's

migration_plan: None: no record type, schema or stored state changes. The background path is enabled by Body.run at boot.

steps: Revert this branch's commit, or decline intake into #196
Or, at runtime, leave engine.background None (inline dispatch)

kill_criteria: A ledger write from two threads at once (a broken hash chain or a lost record) on any test or body
A dispatch recorded twice, or recorded for a mission while its worker still runs
A STOP that no longer terminates a running worker
decision_owner: GREG maintainers for development; Alfonso for the pause ruling and any merge
review_trigger: A founder ruling on pause, the durable job model becoming necessary (workers that outlive a restart), or a concurrency defect; an intake review finding
